statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14668 (PostgreSQL ctid type confusion in selectivity estimator discloses derivative of arbitrary read): the ctid special case in scalarineqsel() did not check that the comparison constant is of type tid, so an operator created by a user could have an arbitrary Datum read as an ItemPointer. PostgreSQL fixed it in 16.15 for major version 16: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14668/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release, and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_16_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/591192e2ec76922f847e39e01d4d4d3ababc5178 (Security: CVE-2026-14668), the backport of master commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/8f0c3d2feb9d7a9905d1ed0122ff1fb2bd3cfb0a, and adds the consttype == TIDOID condition in src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c; it is in tag REL_16_15 and not in REL_16_14. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14668 under 16.15-r0 in its secfixes. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch and the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball, and none of the patches in the APKBUILD at that commit touches selfuncs.c. The fix adds no message string, so we identified each build by the release banner in /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, read from every published postgresql16 package for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0) on x86_64 and aarch64: 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.13 and 16.14, while 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report 16.15 and 16.16. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14668, type confusion in the ctid selectivity estimator that discloses a value derived from arbitrary memory, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14668/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14668. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
